claims.capability: Cashier can add a catalog item by keyword, UPC/SKU search or by scanning its GTIN when compatible scanning hardware/camera is available.
claims.merchant_outcome: Finds the intended item without browsing the entire item grid.
claims.trigger: At POS checkout, search or scan an item identifier.
claims.behavior: Search accepts keyword, UPC or SKU; GTIN scan adds the associated item when a compatible scanner or supported iOS camera is connected.
claims.preconditions: POS app; item identifier associated with catalog entry; supported scanner/camera for scan flow.
claims.qualifiers: US; documented primarily in Square Retail POS guide; Dashboard Virtual Terminal has a separate scan path.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If scan accessory/camera is unsupported or GTIN is not associated, use keyword/UPC/SKU search; docs do not state behavior for ambiguous matches.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: OpenBMT could offer fast local item lookup with scanner and resilient manual search while preserving merchant-controlled item records.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cart lookup does not require Bitcoin settlement; same cashier workflow should serve cash, card and Bitcoin tenders.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Offline/local search helps during connectivity loss but catalog synchronization conflicts may create stale prices or tax rules.
claims.acceptance_test: Given a GTIN linked to an item and a supported scanner, scanning adds that item; keyword, UPC and SKU searches resolve the same item.

claims.capability: Cashier can select an item variation and required or optional modifiers from item details before adding/saving the item.
claims.merchant_outcome: Captures choices such as size and add-ons as part of the sale.
claims.trigger: Adding or editing an item with variations or modifiers.
claims.behavior: The item details screen presents variations and modifier selections; the cashier saves the configured item to cart.
claims.preconditions: Item has configured variations/modifiers; POS supports the relevant mode.
claims.qualifiers: Standard/services and Retail flows differ in save/add-to-cart labels; mode and device details apply.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Required modifier choices must be made; if selection labels truncate, a wider tile layout is documented. Exact handling of unavailable modifiers not covered.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show modifier totals and payment method consequences before commitment, with merchant-editable options.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Item configuration should remain independent of whether the later tender is Lightning Bitcoin, card or cash.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Currency conversion at payment time can make the Bitcoin amount differ from the static USD item amount; quote timing must be visible at tender selection.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure a required variation and modifier, save, and verify the cart preserves both and computes the expected USD subtotal.

claims.capability: Cashier can preselect or change quantity during item configuration before the item is saved.
claims.merchant_outcome: Enters multi-unit sales in one cart action and can correct quantity before committing item details.
claims.trigger: Adding or editing a cart item.
claims.behavior: Quantity bar can preselect a count before adding; item detail +/- controls or numeric field change quantity, then Save commits it.
claims.preconditions: POS checkout item entry.
claims.qualifiers: US Square Retail POS guide; available controls depend on item entry flow.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After saving the cart, the relevant quantity fields are locked and cannot be changed through item details per guide; do not assert other change paths.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Allow transparent correction of an unpaid cart quantity with a clear recalculation trail.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Quantity should be settled in merchant price units; BTC quote is generated only after final cart changes.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Changing quantity after generating an invoice/quote invalidates a payment request; the UI must distinguish cart edits from issued payment requests.
claims.acceptance_test: Set quantity before saving; verify extended line total. After save, test documented lock and expose any alternative edit route explicitly.

claims.capability: Cashier can add optional item notes during checkout; notes can be configured separately for checkout visibility and receipt visibility.
claims.merchant_outcome: Records fulfillment details and can control whether those notes print/show to a buyer.
claims.trigger: Cashier opens item details and enters note; operator adjusts profile/receipt setting.
claims.behavior: Notes may be added before payment; hiding the empty note field does not clear existing notes, which remain read-only. Receipt toggle separately controls display.
claims.preconditions: Item note field enabled for profile; receipt preference configured for desired customer display.
claims.qualifiers: US POS; modes use profile settings; required custom-amount descriptions remain visible.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Notes/descriptions cannot be added after payment; existing hidden notes cannot be edited via hidden field until reenabled.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let merchants choose receipt privacy defaults while retaining a clear order audit trail.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Notes and receipt privacy should work identically across tender types, including Bitcoin.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Do not put sensitive personal data in public receipt or on-chain metadata; keep checkout notes off-chain and access controlled.
claims.acceptance_test: Add note, hide checkout field, confirm saved note remains read-only and independently verify receipt display toggle.

claims.capability: Cashier can adjust a catalog item's price for the current transaction and restore its original price before saving.
claims.merchant_outcome: Handles an authorized one-off price correction without changing the default item price.
claims.trigger: Open item details, enable Price adjustment and enter new price.
claims.behavior: A transaction-specific adjusted price is saved; toggling adjustment off restores catalog price for that transaction.
claims.preconditions: POS item details supports price adjustment; any permission restrictions apply but were not detailed in inspected page.
claims.qualifiers: US Square Retail POS guide; visibility of item details can vary by profile.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Source describes returning to original price before completion; post-payment corrections are not established here.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a logged, reversible price override with reason and merchant-set approval controls.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Apply overrides to USD-denominated cart first, then quote BTC at payment; preserve the quoted amount and expiry.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Price override after quote issuance risks mismatch, so lock quote on confirmed payment request or require re-quote.
claims.acceptance_test: Adjust price and save, verify only current cart changes; turn off adjustment and verify original item price returns.

claims.capability: Cashier can remove an accidentally added item before a sale completes.
claims.merchant_outcome: Corrects the cart before payment.
claims.trigger: Select item and set quantity to zero or swipe/delete; or clear entire cart.
claims.behavior: Individual item removal requires confirmation in documented flow; the entire cart can be cleared from cart menu.
claims.preconditions: Sale is not complete.
claims.qualifiers: US Square Retail POS guide.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Clearing cart removes all current entries; source does not describe undo/restore.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Use an undo affordance and explicit confirmation for destructive cart removal.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Before a Bitcoin invoice is created, cart removal should simply update the payable amount.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: After creating a Lightning invoice, cart edits need to invalidate or cancel the old quote to prevent under/overpayment.
claims.acceptance_test: Remove one line and verify other lines remain; clear cart and verify all lines are removed with confirmation.

claims.capability: Cashier can choose whether identical cart items consolidate to one row with a count or appear as separate rows.
claims.merchant_outcome: Adapts cart readability to high-volume or item-by-item workflows.
claims.trigger: Change cart setting for the device mode.
claims.behavior: Consolidation is on by default in article; disabling it creates separate rows for repeated taps; setting is per mode.
claims.preconditions: POS cart settings access.
claims.qualifiers: US; setting per mode.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Changing the setting affects cart presentation; source does not say whether it modifies already-open carts.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Offer configurable compact/detail cart views while preserving quantity semantics and item-level auditability.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cart presentation should not change payment totals or BTC quote computation.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Merged rows may obscure item-specific tax/discount treatment if line attributes differ; consolidate only semantically identical lines.
claims.acceptance_test: Toggle consolidation off/on and add repeated same item; verify separate rows versus one row with quantity and identical total.

claims.capability: Operator can hide selected item detail controls per profile, while the underlying tax, discount, service-charge settings and saved data remain in effect.
claims.merchant_outcome: Simplifies the screen without silently removing configured pricing behavior or notes.
claims.trigger: Toggle item detail visibility options in POS Checkout > Order Entry.
claims.behavior: Visibility options include notes, fulfillment, taxes, discounts and service charges; hiding affects display only and does not disable rules, change totals or delete data.
claims.preconditions: Profile access and supported Square POS mode.
claims.qualifiers: US; these visibility settings are profile-level; per-item behavior may be global separately.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Hidden existing notes remain read-only; hidden controls may make correction less direct.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make compact cashier layouts configurable while always exposing an inspectable breakdown before payment.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Keep tax/discount math visible in total breakdown independent of settlement currency.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Hidden pricing components can make BTC conversion seem opaque; show both USD subtotal and final quoted BTC amount.
claims.acceptance_test: Hide each supported detail control, verify totals and stored settings are unchanged, then restore control and inspect value.

claims.capability: Cashier can apply a configured percentage or dollar discount manually, subject to item and sale eligibility rules.
claims.merchant_outcome: Honors promotions or discretionary price reductions during checkout.
claims.trigger: Choose a preset discount in the sale or item flow.
claims.behavior: Percentage can apply sale-wide or to items; fixed amount normally applies sale-wide except automatic discount configuration; each specific discount can be used once per sale.
claims.preconditions: Discount configured; cashier has checkout permission to apply restricted discounts.
claims.qualifiers: US POS; advanced discount rules can restrict eligible items even when selected.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Ineligible items remain undiscounted; cart indicates exclusions. Source says a specific discount cannot be applied twice.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Present eligibility and per-line effect before finalizing a discount, with a reason log.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Compute discount in USD cart accounting before conversion into BTC amount.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Rounding at BTC denomination may produce fractional differences; retain canonical USD total and disclose rounding method.
claims.acceptance_test: Apply eligible and ineligible discount to mixed cart; verify only allowed lines change and duplicate application is prevented.

claims.capability: Configured automatic discounts can trigger when sale rules such as eligible items, quantity, customer group, date/time or minimum spend are satisfied.
claims.merchant_outcome: Applies promotions without requiring cashier to remember each condition.
claims.trigger: Cart/customer/time conditions match an automatic discount.
claims.behavior: Discount is inserted automatically when conditions are met; advanced rules can target categories/items, quantity/BOGO, groups, schedules and minimum spend.
claims.preconditions: Discount configured, automation enabled, current POS app; customer-group discount requires adding group customer where specified.
claims.qualifiers: US; discount capabilities depend on configuration and app version.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If automatic discount fails to apply, support article suggests updating Square app; excluded items never receive it.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show a concise explanation for each applied or missed promotion to reduce cashier disputes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Discount rules should be evaluated from cart data before payment rail selection.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Customer group rules involve identity data; avoid making Bitcoin access conditional on identity beyond legal requirements.
claims.acceptance_test: Create quantity and time-window promotions; verify eligible cart auto-applies inside window/threshold and not outside.

claims.capability: Merchant can exclude an item or variation from all discounts, and the cart indicates that the item is excluded.
claims.merchant_outcome: Prevents protected products, gift cards or loss leaders from receiving discounts.
claims.trigger: Operator marks item/variation excluded; cashier adds it to a cart with a discount.
claims.behavior: Excluded products receive no manual or automatic discounts; cart-level discounts skip excluded items and apply only to eligible items; cart flags the excluded line.
claims.preconditions: Item-level eligibility configured.
claims.qualifiers: US; item or variation-level setting.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Discount may still apply to eligible neighboring items; do not infer discount rejection for entire cart.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide explicit line-level explanation and override governance for excluded products.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Apply exclusions before tender selection so Bitcoin does not create a separate promotion path.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: If item and sale totals are rounded into satoshis, preserve which lines were eligible in receipt evidence.
claims.acceptance_test: Mix excluded and eligible items and apply sale-wide and automatic discounts; verify exclusion flag and eligible-only discount.

claims.capability: Discount configuration supports minimum spend, scheduling/date ranges and a maximum discount value when configured.
claims.merchant_outcome: Limits promotion timing and exposure to intended thresholds.
claims.trigger: Configure discount rules in Dashboard/POS.
claims.behavior: Minimum spend, date/time schedule and max value can constrain applicability/value; automatic/manual setting controls whether cashier selects it, not rule capabilities.
claims.preconditions: Supported discount type and advanced rules available in account UI.
claims.qualifiers: US; source notes specific amount options and rules vary by setup; exact combination support is not exhaustively established.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Discounts outside schedule or below threshold are not eligible; multiple discounts with maximum values have caps only on discounts configured with one.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview total discount exposure and reasons for non-eligibility as a merchant configures a promotion.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Thresholds should be calculated in the store's accounting currency before BTC quoting.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: If Bitcoin quote changes while a promotion is evaluated, avoid applying thresholds to volatile BTC rather than fixed USD cart values.
claims.acceptance_test: Test cart below/above minimum, inside/outside schedule and max cap; confirm displayed discount matches configured rules.

claims.capability: Operator can reorder, disable and re-enable payment types shown in the POS checkout screen.
claims.merchant_outcome: Prioritizes common tenders and removes choices a location does not accept.
claims.trigger: Modify payment type settings and preview checkout screen.
claims.behavior: Enabled tenders can be reordered; disabled tenders can be restored; edits on one device reflect on other devices linked to the location, including Retail/Restaurants apps.
claims.preconditions: Account and settings permission.
claims.qualifiers: US; linked same-location device synchronization; defaults include cash and check.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Disabling a tender removes it from checkout until re-enabled; source indicates preview function but does not describe propagation delay.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let each merchant choose tender order and visibility without making a payment intermediary mandatory.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Make Bitcoin an independently toggleable tender with merchant-controlled placement and no required fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Too many tender options increase cashier friction; defaults should be concise and merchant-editable.
claims.acceptance_test: Disable and reorder Bitcoin/cash/card options; verify display order and availability on linked location devices.

claims.capability: Square POS can record cash, checks, third-party gift cards and other tenders as organizational records without Square processing or transferring those funds.
claims.merchant_outcome: Keeps non-Square-exchanged tender records with sales activity while money exchanges directly between buyer and merchant.
claims.trigger: Choose a configured cash, check or other-tender type at checkout.
claims.behavior: Square records the tender amount; it does not process those funds and money is exchanged directly by seller and customer.
claims.preconditions: Tender enabled in checkout settings.
claims.qualifiers: US; no fee for those tender types according to page; recording is not equivalent to payment confirmation by Square.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Merchant must ensure the external tender actually changed hands; source does not describe correction workflows.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make native cash and other noncustodial tenders first-class and distinguish recorded evidence from processor-confirmed settlement.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Support merchant-self-hosted Bitcoin receipt while clearly separating transaction confirmation from book-entry record; no forced fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Self-hosted acceptance shifts confirmation, price risk, custody and refund responsibilities to merchant.
claims.acceptance_test: Record cash and other tender; confirm ledger labels as merchant-recorded and does not imply third-party settlement; test merchant Bitcoin node path separately.

claims.capability: A POS sale may be completed with multiple tender amounts as long as the full sale balance is processed within the time window.
claims.merchant_outcome: Allows customers to divide a bill across payment methods or payers.
claims.trigger: Select Split Amount and process successive payment portions.
claims.behavior: Sale is incomplete until no balance remains; split must complete within five minutes or the bill may time out and prior processed payments may be voided.
claims.preconditions: Supported Square app/mobile/hardware or Virtual Terminal; for connected Square Terminal, card-involved splits are unavailable.
claims.qualifiers: US; device integration limitation applies.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Timeout may void earlier portions; restart/recovery path is not fully described. Each subsequent tender may have separate failure outcomes.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show outstanding balance, timer and reversibility state for each tender before starting a split.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Permit mixed Bitcoin and cash/card settlement when merchant opts in, with each portion finalized and no processor-required custody.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin payments are final and cannot be reversed like card authorizations; timeout handling must not imply a Bitcoin payment can be voided after network settlement.
claims.acceptance_test: Complete two-tender split inside five minutes; simulate timeout and verify status/reconciliation for already processed portion and any void.

claims.capability: Restaurant mode supports splitting checks by item or seat under certain plan/flow requirements, while payment splitting may be amount-only.
claims.merchant_outcome: Enables restaurants to allocate a shared table bill by diners or items when the feature is available.
claims.trigger: Use split check in restaurant order/payment workflow.
claims.behavior: Item/seat splitting requires Square for Restaurants Plus or Premium and New order and pay; article notes payment splits may be by amount only, and voiding a previously split item can recombine it.
claims.preconditions: Full service/quick service/bar mode or Restaurants app; plan/flow prerequisites for item splits.
claims.qualifiers: US; Square for Restaurants Plus/Premium or Square Plus/Premium with advanced restaurant capabilities; item splitting/recombining specifically requires New order and pay.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Voiding previously split item can recombine fractions; specific edge behavior and device restrictions need source-level follow-up.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make check splitting work consistently across plans with visible seat/item allocation and auditable recombination.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: If mixed payment is supported, item/seat allocations should remain stable regardless of settlement method.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Per-seat Lightning invoices add QR handoffs and may delay table close; table-level payment and allocation could be simpler.
claims.acceptance_test: On a qualifying Restaurant plan, split by seat and item, void one fraction, verify recombination and amounts; compare amount-only payment split behavior.

claims.capability: Operator can enable offline acceptance and choose whether to accept cash plus card or cash only during outages.
claims.merchant_outcome: Continues recording selected tenders during an internet or Square service interruption.
claims.trigger: Enable offline payments at mode/device settings; network/server unavailable.
claims.behavior: POS stores offline card transactions in app and continues cash; settings can allow card and cash or cash only. Offline behavior is automatically enabled on all devices unless opted out per current article’s dated rollout.
claims.preconditions: Supported POS mode/device; offline payment enabled; device was prepared and applicable setting permits outage type.
claims.qualifiers: US; docs describe rollout in March/April 2026 and device-specific differences; feature not universal to all tenders.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Offline card charges remain pending and may later decline/dispute; merchant accepts risk and Square cannot provide contact info for affected buyers.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Offer merchant-controlled local payment continuity for cash and self-hosted Bitcoin with explicit pending/confirmed state.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A merchant operated Lightning node could accept payments during processor outage if connectivity to Lightning remains; alternatively on-chain Bitcoin can be accepted with confirmation policy.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin Lightning itself requires network connectivity and channel liquidity; local POS being offline does not guarantee Bitcoin receipt. Offline card risk is distinct from Bitcoin finality.
claims.acceptance_test: Disconnect POS from Square while retaining/losing internet separately; verify supported offline tenders, local pending status, and clear operator risk warning.

claims.capability: Offline mode excludes several tenders including EBT/SNAP, Afterpay, Cash App Pay, Square Gift Cards, Tap to Pay and manual card entry.
claims.merchant_outcome: Cashier knows which payment methods remain usable when offline mode is active.
claims.trigger: Attempt to take payment while POS has no connection.
claims.behavior: The listed tenders are unavailable for offline payment; operator may select cash-only acceptance.
claims.preconditions: Offline mode and supported device.
claims.qualifiers: US; list reflects cited support article and may change; card brands/devices have separate acceptance qualifications.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Use available cash/offline card or reconnect; docs do not describe an offline queuing mechanism for excluded tenders.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Display unavailable tender states before the customer commits to a payment method.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Show clearly whether merchant-run Bitcoin wallet accepts payments under current network conditions rather than suggesting POS offline means Bitcoin offline.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Third-party network or processor outages may still affect Bitcoin wallet payment despite independent custody.
claims.acceptance_test: Enter offline state and attempt each documented unavailable tender; verify clear unavailable message and alternative tender guidance.

claims.capability: Offline card payments must be uploaded after reconnection within a hardware-specific deadline; pending payments expire if not uploaded within 72 hours.
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can recover locally stored payments, with a defined upload deadline and expired state.
claims.trigger: Device reconnects after accepting offline payments.
claims.behavior: Register, Terminal and Handheld have up to 72 hours to reconnect/upload; 24 hours is recommended. Certain readers/stands permit 24-hour offline acceptance sessions and require reconnection every 24 hours; pending payments expire after 72 hours and cannot be retrieved or reprocessed.
claims.preconditions: Supported hardware; offline transactions pending locally.
claims.qualifiers: US; precise cutoff differs by hardware. Page also references an automatic reconnection/process deadline; check hardware-specific paragraph.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Expired transactions cannot be recovered or reprocessed; late uploads may expose merchant to declines/chargebacks.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide durable local receipts, operator reminders and recovery exports before expiration.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A merchant-controlled Bitcoin wallet can preserve signed transaction evidence without Square upload window, though settlement still depends on network and wallet availability.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Local Bitcoin transaction records do not ensure a payment was broadcast/confirmed; durable state and retry policy are still needed.
claims.acceptance_test: Accept test offline card payments on each supported hardware class, reconnect before and after deadlines, verify state transitions and irrecoverable-expiry message.

claims.capability: Offline payments appear pending in POS history while offline and resolve to completed or declined after reconnection or Square service restoration.
claims.merchant_outcome: Cashier can distinguish provisional offline acceptance from a confirmed payment outcome.
claims.trigger: Review payment history offline or after service restoration.
claims.behavior: Pending offline transactions are viewable in POS app only; completed transactions are visible in app and Dashboard; after reconnect they show completed or declined.
claims.preconditions: Offline payment exists and appropriate transaction permissions.
claims.qualifiers: US; pending visibility is app-only.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Declined payment may require contacting buyer, but Square says it cannot provide contact information or contact customer for seller for declined/expired offline charges.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Use explicit provisional/final states with a follow-up queue for unresolved payments.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Show Bitcoin invoice paid/settled only after verified Lightning receipt, separate from a locally created request or unverified buyer message.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment state terminology must not equate card authorization, Lightning settlement and on-chain confirmations.
claims.acceptance_test: Observe pending offline payment locally; reconnect and verify completed/declined transition and Dashboard visibility rules.

claims.capability: Eligible Square sellers can accept Lightning Bitcoin at POS through a QR invoice; on Register (2nd generation) customer may initiate from buyer display and can pay by QR or NFC tap.
claims.merchant_outcome: Offers a Bitcoin tender alongside other checkout methods with QR/NFC customer interaction.
claims.trigger: Cashier enters amount or selects catalog/menu item, chooses Bitcoin; or customer selects Bitcoin on supported buyer display.
claims.behavior: Square displays Lightning QR for buyer wallet; Register 2nd generation also supports buyer-facing flow and NFC tap. Latest Square POS app required.
claims.preconditions: Feature enabled/eligible; current app; US location outside New York; buyer uses Lightning-enabled wallet; NFC specifically requires Register (2nd generation).
claims.qualifiers: Square page says available across all POS modes for Bitcoin payment; buyer-facing and NFC paths limited to Register (2nd generation), not Terminal/Stand/mobile.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Bitcoin payments can take up to five minutes; if unresolved, decline and create a new cart with current exchange rate. Manual Complete payment action is seller-discretionary and Square does not reimburse if payment was not received.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide standards-based merchant-controlled Lightning invoice creation and independently verifiable settlement without company eligibility gating.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: This is a direct Bitcoin tender example; OpenBMT can preserve Bitcoin-first settlement and merchant keys while supporting QR and optionally NFC.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Square’s streamlined buyer UX depends on company-controlled eligibility, wallet, quotes and settlement choices; self-custody shifts operational security and liquidity burdens to merchant.
claims.acceptance_test: On eligible non-NY account with current app, complete QR Lightning payment; separately verify buyer-facing/NFC path only on Register 2nd gen and reject unsupported hardware claims.

claims.capability: Bitcoin checkout prices goods in USD and converts to Bitcoin at transaction-time market rate; POS Bitcoin transactions have a current equivalent maximum $600 and $20,000 daily limit.
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant retains familiar USD pricing while customer sees a current BTC amount subject to cap.
claims.trigger: Bitcoin is selected as tender after cart is assembled.
claims.behavior: Bitcoin amount is based on USD cart value and current market price; per-transaction and daily caps constrain acceptance.
claims.preconditions: Bitcoin enabled and eligible; account/location limits apply.
claims.qualifiers: US support page as accessed Nov. 17, 2026; caps and fee terms may change; source states USD-settled new eligible sellers default.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Over-limit purchase requires another payment method or splitting if supported; exact split policy is not documented in this Bitcoin page. Quote time limit five minutes documented separately.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Offer merchant-set fixed BTC pricing or transparent quote lock duration in addition to USD-based amounts.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin-first merchant may choose fixed sats pricing and own exchange-rate policy; USD display can remain optional.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Fixed fiat-priced carts protect merchant margins but expose buyer to price volatility; fixed sat pricing exposes merchant to volatility.
claims.acceptance_test: Verify displayed BTC amount is based on checkout quote and reject individual amount above current documented cap; ensure cap is configurable/versioned in implementation.

claims.capability: Bitcoin held in a Square Bitcoin wallet is held by Square/Block as custodian for the seller; when withdrawn to an external or self-custody wallet, the seller controls that external wallet.
claims.merchant_outcome: Clarifies who controls Bitcoin while it remains in Square wallet and after withdrawal.
claims.trigger: Seller holds Bitcoin in Square wallet or withdraws Bitcoin to an external wallet.
claims.behavior: Square’s wallet help explicitly states Square is custodian of funds held in the Square wallet. Withdrawal to an external/self-custody wallet transfers control to the seller, who becomes responsible for wallet security and recovery information.
claims.preconditions: Eligible US seller with Square Bitcoin wallet; withdrawal feature configured and available.
claims.qualifiers: Wallet unavailable to sellers in New York and US territories. This claim concerns custody while funds are held in Square wallet and control after withdrawal; it does not claim merchant-key settlement at POS. Terms say Bitcoin acquired via Square Bitcoin is custodial and title remains with seller.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Square account protections apply while funds are in Square custody; external-wallet recovery is seller responsibility. Deposits into Square wallet conflict across reviewed docs and are not asserted here.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make key custody explicit and offer direct settlement to merchant-controlled wallet without company account/approval dependency.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: OpenBMT target is merchant-controlled keys from receipt onward, without mandatory custody; third-party custody can remain an explicit opt-in route.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Custody can provide account recovery support but places withdrawal access and timing under provider controls; self-custody transfers key backup and security responsibility to merchant.
claims.acceptance_test: Verify whether the merchant controls signing keys for funds at each state: Square-held wallet balance vs withdrawn external wallet; assert custody boundary and recovery responsibility in UI.

claims.capability: Square POS allows seller to manually mark a Bitcoin payment complete if buyer wallet says paid but POS confirmation is delayed; unresolved payments over five minutes are declined and need a new cart/quote.
claims.merchant_outcome: Provides a way to issue a receipt when payment confirmation is delayed, while warning seller bears risk.
claims.trigger: Buyer reports transaction confirmed but Square POS is slow to confirm, or payment waits beyond timeout.
claims.behavior: Seller may select Complete payment from menu at their discretion; Square disclaims reimbursement for payment not actually received. At five minutes, payment declines and new cart required at refreshed exchange rate.
claims.preconditions: Square Bitcoin checkout active; seller can inspect payer evidence; current app.
claims.qualifiers: US Lightning QR/NFC flows; exact node-level verification semantics not detailed.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Manual completion can create a false paid record if seller's independent verification is wrong; expired quote cannot simply continue.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Use independently verifiable merchant wallet settlement and clearly distinguish buyer-side screenshot from received funds.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: OpenBMT should treat confirmed invoice receipt as source of truth and provide expert/manual override only with signed reconciliation evidence.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Avoiding provider confirmation service increases merchant responsibility to run a reliable node and monitor channel/payment state.
claims.acceptance_test: Simulate buyer app paid while merchant node has no settlement; ensure system does not finalize automatically; test timeout and new invoice generation.

claims.capability: Square POS refunds Bitcoin sales only via a store gift card for the equivalent USD amount; staff selects items or amount and refund reason in mobile/tablet POS.
claims.merchant_outcome: Allows a merchant to compensate a Bitcoin payer with store credit, while the Bitcoin payment itself remains final.
claims.trigger: Open transaction in POS and issue a Bitcoin refund.
claims.behavior: Choose items or amount, enter dollar amount and reason, confirm; customer receives gift card usable at the store, described as the same amount of Bitcoin as original payment in gift-card form.
claims.preconditions: Refund via Square POS mobile device/tablet; setup automatically enrolls seller in Square e-gift cards; Dashboard refund unavailable per related invoice doc, but POS page describes POS path.
claims.qualifiers: US; refund medium is store gift card, not Bitcoin transfer to buyer wallet or reversal.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: No blockchain reversal; chargebacks/disputes not supported; merchant and customer must resolve other adjustments directly.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Allow merchant-selected refund destination, including a new noncustodial Bitcoin payment, while retaining clear original-currency accounting.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin finality should not prohibit seller-initiated refunds; OpenBMT can send a new Lightning/on-chain payment to customer or issue store credit at merchant discretion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Refund to buyer requires verified destination and may use a different exchange rate; store credit avoids address handling but constrains customer.
claims.acceptance_test: Accept Bitcoin sale, issue partial and item refund, verify gift-card amount and reason; test optional direct wallet refund separately and record exchange rate.

claims.capability: Square records Bitcoin payments in ordinary POS sales reporting and identifies them as Bitcoin; checkout page says eligible Bitcoin payers receive Square Loyalty points when seller uses Loyalty.
claims.merchant_outcome: Integrates Bitcoin sales into existing seller transaction and loyalty flow.
claims.trigger: Bitcoin payment confirms for sale where merchant has Square Loyalty.
claims.behavior: Sales appear in reporting marked Bitcoin; customer receives loyalty points when program is active.
claims.preconditions: Square Bitcoin payment accepted; Loyalty program active for loyalty behavior.
claims.qualifiers: US Square product behavior. Reporting is adjacent to cashier checkout, but covered because it affects tender outcome; detailed reporting mechanics excluded by other Square scope.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Reporting details and points correction behavior are not documented in checkout article.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide exportable, neutral tender records with merchant-defined rewards integrations.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin sale can remain an ordinary sale event while payment rail metadata identifies Lightning settlement; loyalty should not depend on custodial account.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Customer rewards may reveal payment identity and link activity; minimize unnecessary personal data.
claims.acceptance_test: Complete Bitcoin sale with and without active Loyalty; verify sale marked Bitcoin and points behavior only when program active.

claims.capability: Tax settings allow merchant to apply a named rate to all taxable items or selected items at chosen locations, and optionally apply it to custom amounts.
claims.merchant_outcome: Cart taxes taxable items under merchant’s selected rule.
claims.trigger: Create tax and select items/locations; POS then calculates order tax.
claims.behavior: Tax settings allow merchant to apply a named rate to all taxable items or selected items at chosen locations, and optionally apply it to custom amounts.
claims.preconditions: Tax is created and item is taxable; relevant location configured.
claims.qualifiers: US; Square says merchant remains responsible for correct configuration, collection and remittance; no tax advice.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Non-taxable items do not receive automatic tax; exact jurisdictional applicability is merchant responsibility.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Set up clear item-level tax rules and show affected lines before tender.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin tender should not alter the merchant’s configured taxable base.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Tax laws vary; do not hardcode jurisdiction rules as Bitcoin-specific behavior.
claims.acceptance_test: Set tax for selected item only, add taxable and non-taxable items plus custom amount; verify line tax application.

claims.capability: Merchant can choose additive tax shown as a separate receipt line or inclusive tax contained in item price.
claims.merchant_outcome: Controls whether displayed item price includes tax or tax is added at checkout.
claims.trigger: Choose calculation method when creating tax.
claims.behavior: Merchant can choose additive tax shown as a separate receipt line or inclusive tax contained in item price.
claims.preconditions: Tax configuration access; applicable item tax exists.
claims.qualifiers: US POS; receipt presentation differs by calculation method.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Changing tax method affects checkout totals/presentation; no advice on legally appropriate method.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show pre-tax base, tax and total in receipt preview for both modes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Present the tax amount in accounting currency before showing any Bitcoin quote.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Inclusive pricing may obscure base amount; display breakdown for transparent conversion.
claims.acceptance_test: Create same rate as additive and inclusive; compare line and final total and receipt representation.

claims.capability: Merchant can configure an exemption rule for a tax; tax rules may reduce/exempt applicable cart items.
claims.merchant_outcome: Applies configured exemption or reduction when rule conditions match.
claims.trigger: Create tax exemption/reduction rule and add qualifying item to cart.
claims.behavior: Merchant can configure an exemption rule for a tax; tax rules may reduce/exempt applicable cart items.
claims.preconditions: A sales tax exists; rules configured in Dashboard; supported POS app current.
claims.qualifiers: US; tax rules apply to cart items, not item modifiers; category rules follow category membership.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Incorrect setup can miscalculate tax; Square disclaims accuracy/advice.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Explain which rule caused a line to be exempt and make calculation reviewable.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Tax treatment should be independent of whether settlement uses Bitcoin or fiat tender.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Avoid suggesting Bitcoin payment creates tax exemption; merchant needs compliant records.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure qualifying exemption and compare qualifying item with nonqualifying item and modifier.

claims.capability: Tipping settings let merchant ask for a tip before payment on supported counter hardware, or move prompt after payment; customer can choose configured options/custom amount/no tip.
claims.merchant_outcome: Collects optional tip while customer remains at checkout.
claims.trigger: Customer reaches tip step in checkout.
claims.behavior: Tipping settings let merchant ask for a tip before payment on supported counter hardware, or move prompt after payment; customer can choose configured options/custom amount/no tip.
claims.preconditions: Tipping enabled; hardware and flow support chosen setting.
claims.qualifiers: US; before-payment setting applies Register/Terminal/Stand; prompt changes payment order and may expose non-card tenders through All payment types.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Printed sign/tip incompatible with NFC contactless; sign-on-receipt unavailable if ask-before-payment enabled.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let merchant set tip prompt timing and make no-tip choice equally easy.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin customers should see equivalent optional tip flow and final sats/USD breakdown.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Do not make tip calculation depend on payment rail; custom tip can require re-quote if total changes.
claims.acceptance_test: Test before/after tip prompt on supported hardware for card and non-card tenders, including no tip.

claims.capability: Merchant can configure smart or percentage tip presets, custom amounts and whether tip is calculated before or after tax; round-up option has transaction thresholds.
claims.merchant_outcome: Provides suggested tip values and calculation policy.
claims.trigger: Set tipping options; customer selects suggestion or custom amount.
claims.behavior: Merchant can configure smart or percentage tip presets, custom amounts and whether tip is calculated before or after tax; round-up option has transaction thresholds.
claims.preconditions: Tipping enabled; round-up supported only on listed iPad/iPhone/Terminal/Handheld/Android.
claims.qualifiers: US; Smart amounts documented as under $10: no tip/$1/$2/$3; $10+: no tip/15/20/25%; round-up under $20 next dollar, $20+ next $5.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Custom amounts can be disabled; setting percentages all 0% results in custom/no-tip choices only.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make preset math and before/after-tax basis explicit to reduce pressure and miscalculation.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Calculate USD tip first then translate payment amount under displayed Bitcoin quote.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Exchange-rate changes and sat rounding can cause a displayed tip amount mismatch if quote is regenerated.
claims.acceptance_test: Test threshold values and verify tip-before-tax and tip-after-tax totals; verify custom disabled and round-up availability.

claims.capability: Signed open checks can settle automatically after 36 hours with zero tip if not manually settled; printed-receipt tips must be entered in that window.
claims.merchant_outcome: Closes payment state after tip opportunity expires.
claims.trigger: Open signed check awaits tip settlement.
claims.behavior: Signed open checks can settle automatically after 36 hours with zero tip if not manually settled; printed-receipt tips must be entered in that window.
claims.preconditions: Tipping enabled; payment awaiting settlement.
claims.qualifiers: US; standard/restaurant modes; team member default settlement scope limited to own processed payments.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After timeout default zero tip; manual/bulk POS settlement needed earlier.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide reminders and visible deadline before automatic zero-tip settlement.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin payments are final at settlement and should not inherit card authorization/tip settlement semantics without clear disclosure.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Separating tip from finalized Bitcoin base payment may require a second Lightning payment.
claims.acceptance_test: Create signed open check, add tip before 36 hours and verify settlement; review timeout behavior in test account.

claims.capability: After successful payment, cashier can offer printed, texted or emailed receipt; itemized receipt includes quantities, discounts and applicable taxes.
claims.merchant_outcome: Provides buyer payment evidence in a selected channel.
claims.trigger: Payment succeeds and receipt screen appears, or cashier prints from POS.
claims.behavior: After successful payment, cashier can offer printed, texted or emailed receipt; itemized receipt includes quantities, discounts and applicable taxes.
claims.preconditions: Transactions permission; compatible printer for print; skip receipt screen must be disabled to prompt buyer.
claims.qualifiers: US; email may be auto-sent to a previously opted-in address; receipt screen can use entered customer contact.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If skip screen enabled, customer is not prompted to choose print/text/email/no receipt; declined card receipt is a separate printer setting.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Offer printed or digital receipt with minimum necessary personal data and itemized totals.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Receipt should identify Bitcoin tender and preserve USD and BTC value without exposing wallet secrets.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Email/phone collection creates privacy obligations; avoid requiring identity for noncustodial payment.
claims.acceptance_test: Complete payment with receipt prompt enabled; verify print/text/email paths and itemized quantity, discount, tax.

claims.capability: Operator can skip receipt prompt; opted-in customers then receive digital receipts automatically when available and customers are not offered receipt channel choice.
claims.merchant_outcome: Speeds checkout for high-volume counters.
claims.trigger: Enable Skip receipt screen on a device.
claims.behavior: Operator can skip receipt prompt; opted-in customers then receive digital receipts automatically when available and customers are not offered receipt channel choice.
claims.preconditions: Setting is device-local on POS iOS/Android.
claims.qualifiers: US; rewards may be applied automatically where available; additional receipt printing only supported on select Terminal 2nd generation Android rollout.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Customer cannot choose print/text/email/no receipt at checkout when prompt skipped.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Allow faster checkout with a merchant-controlled receipt preference and later access to proof.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin receipt proof should remain available even if cashier skips immediate receipt selection.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Automatic digital receipts may link purchases to customer identity; provide privacy-conscious defaults.
claims.acceptance_test: Enable skip on one device and verify no prompt, automatic receipt to opted-in customer, and another device remains independently configured.

claims.capability: Cashier can refund all items, selected items, or a specified amount from a linked Square card payment, with a reason.
claims.merchant_outcome: Returns value for all or part of an itemized sale.
claims.trigger: Locate original transaction and select items or amount in Issue refund.
claims.behavior: Select all items, specific items, or amount, then choose refund method and reason; custom amount transaction refunds can be up to sale total.
claims.preconditions: Transactions permission; linked Square payment and supported payment type.
claims.qualifiers: US; standard card payment flow is documented; Bitcoin and some other rails use separate rules.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Refund payment methods and processing times vary by tender; refund cannot be canceled after submission.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Support itemized partial refunds with transparent source and status.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: For Bitcoin, allow merchant to issue separate Bitcoin payment or store credit while reflecting the original USD accounting amount.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Refund is a new payment on Bitcoin network, not reversal; address, rate and liquidity must be handled safely.
claims.acceptance_test: Test full, selected-item and amount refund on linked card sale; verify amount, reason, tax/discount accounting and customer outcome.

claims.capability: Submitted refunds generally cannot be canceled, with at most one refund cancellation per transaction under the documented rule.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reduces ability to reverse accidental refunds after submission.
claims.trigger: Attempt to cancel or refund same transaction multiple times.
claims.behavior: Submitted refunds generally cannot be canceled, with at most one refund cancellation per transaction under the documented rule.
claims.preconditions: Refund cancellation feature supported for payment.
claims.qualifiers: US; check exact page UI for payment method/transaction state before implementation.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Wrong transaction selection is consequential; refund cannot be canceled after submission as described in article.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Require explicit destination and amount confirmation before issuing refund and provide clear pending status.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: For Bitcoin return, confirm buyer destination before broadcasting and treat refund as new payment with cancellable pre-send step only.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Irreversible payments need stronger confirmation; cancellation after broadcast may be impossible.
claims.acceptance_test: Attempt to cancel submitted refund and verify one-cancellation-per-transaction rule and resulting status.

claims.capability: Merchant-created custom payment methods can be selected at POS and may capture an optional tip or note when cashier records the external payment.
claims.merchant_outcome: Records a configured external tender in the Square POS flow.
claims.trigger: Create custom payment method and activate it on POS; cashier selects it at charge.
claims.behavior: Merchant-created custom payment methods can be selected at POS and may capture an optional tip or note when cashier records the external payment.
claims.preconditions: Method enabled for POS; optional tip capture configured.
claims.qualifiers: US; amounts appear in reports as Other (report detail excluded from broader scope).
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Square records the transaction; custom method represents external transaction and should not imply Square processed it.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let merchant define external tender labels and capture a note with clear verification state.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant can label a self-hosted Bitcoin method and record external settlement; OpenBMT should natively support verified Lightning receipt without custody intermediary.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Manual custom tender logging can falsely indicate paid; integrate wallet receipt verification while retaining merchant-defined rails.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure custom Bitcoin method, process recorded tender and compare with verified wallet settlement event; UI must distinguish recorded versus verified.

claims.capability: Square-processed POS/Dashboard payments can be refunded within one year of original transaction date; after that, refund must be outside Square.
claims.merchant_outcome: Defines in-product refund eligibility window.
claims.trigger: Issue refund on a Square-processed payment.
claims.behavior: Payments processed through Square can be refunded from Dashboard or POS within one year; later refunds need external handling.
claims.preconditions: Transactions permission; payment type supported.
claims.qualifiers: US; explicit source for standard Square payments.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After one year use an external refund method and document it.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Display refund deadline at transaction lookup and guide alternative documentation.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Record Bitcoin return policy separately; final Bitcoin payment can still be followed by a new payment regardless of original platform window.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin returns are new payments and destination/rate risks remain even when no platform deadline applies.
claims.acceptance_test: Try refund inside and after one year; confirm eligibility boundary and alternative workflow.

claims.capability: Refund processing fees are not returned; Square takes refund funds from available Square balance, or linked bank if balance is insufficient.
claims.merchant_outcome: Shows merchant economic and funding source effect of refund.
claims.trigger: Refund a Square processed payment.
claims.behavior: Square retains original processing fee; refund amount comes from balance or bank account.
claims.preconditions: Square processed payment; linked funding source configured.
claims.qualifiers: US general refunds; specific rail terms may differ.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Insufficient balance may draw linked bank; exact timing/notification depends account.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview refund cost and funding source before final confirmation.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Avoid processor fee dependence for Bitcoin refunds; show network fees and merchant-funded payment explicitly.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin refunds can incur network fees and different amount at current rate.
claims.acceptance_test: Issue refund with low balance in sandbox and verify displayed source, fee treatment, and ledger debit.

claims.capability: Square can record refunds for cash, checks and other tender within one year as an organizational record, but Square does not process the money or send refund notifications.
claims.merchant_outcome: Maintains bookkeeping entry for direct merchant-buyer refund.
claims.trigger: Select non-Square tender refund in transaction history.
claims.behavior: Seller returns funds directly; Square records refund; no fee for recording and no email notification.
claims.preconditions: External tender transaction; one-year window.
claims.qualifiers: US; applies cash/check/other tender.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Merchant must separately communicate and deliver funds.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Distinguish external refund record from verified money return.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Treat merchant-controlled Bitcoin refund as a new outbound payment with receipt proof, distinct from a recorded refund entry.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Merchant takes responsibility for external transfer and notification.
claims.acceptance_test: Record cash/other tender refund and verify ledger status does not claim Square processed funds.

claims.capability: Refund flow lets seller select itemized items or a specific amount; Square help directs refund amount selection but does not document detailed POS tax recalculation in this reviewed article.
claims.merchant_outcome: Lets seller return a sale amount while keeping refund scope tied to items or amount.
claims.trigger: Select refunded item(s) or a dollar amount.
claims.behavior: Documented UI offers itemized or amount refund; tax inclusion/recalculation rules are not specified in the support flow reviewed.
claims.preconditions: Linked Square payment and refund permission.
claims.qualifiers: US; separate legal payment terms state refunds/adjustments must include associated taxes required to be refunded; terms differ from POS help presentation.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Do not assume itemized refund automatically determines legally correct tax treatment without checking transaction tax and applicable law.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show original tax allocation and tax amount in refund preview; let merchant reconcile legally required tax.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin refund accounting should preserve original USD tax amount and separately show sats sent.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Changing BTC market price can make refunded BTC value differ from original USD tax value.
claims.acceptance_test: Refund taxable item and verify exact tax amount/recalculation against original receipt and configured tax; mark any mismatch for merchant review.

claims.capability: When a Square card payment is canceled, interrupted or declined, it may appear as a pending card charge; Square sends void notification to issuer and issuer controls release of hold.
claims.merchant_outcome: Explains why buyer can see a temporary hold without completed merchant payment.
claims.trigger: Card payment fails/cancels or becomes void.
claims.behavior: If transaction absent from payment history but shown on statement, it is pending not actual charge; Square notifies bank of void and bank releases hold.
claims.preconditions: Card transaction canceled/interrupted/declined.
claims.qualifiers: US; bank release timing may take a few business days and is issuer-controlled.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Check transaction history/status report; contact issuer if hold remains.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Give cashier and customer clear “pending hold, no completed sale” receipt and issuer follow-up guidance.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin Lightning invoice expiration should clearly show unpaid/expired instead of pending card authorization state.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Lightning invoice status does not use card-bank hold semantics; separate state model.
claims.acceptance_test: Simulate canceled authorization and verify POS status, no completed payment record, and customer explanation.

claims.capability: Merchant can void an open Restaurant ticket or check with a configured reason when order is incorrect or not yet prepared; void is recorded in Dashboard without a payment record.
claims.merchant_outcome: Removes erroneous unprepared food/drink from a working check.
claims.trigger: Select open ticket/check, choose Void and reason.
claims.behavior: Open ticket voiding records reason and void in Dashboard; no payment record created.
claims.preconditions: Open Checks enabled; void reasons configured.
claims.qualifiers: US; Restaurant modes; check void of item vs entire check flows differ.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Void applies before food/drink prepared or delivered; post-prep removal uses comp instead.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make void/comp distinction and reason visible before action.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: OpenBMT order state should be independent from payment rail; void unpaid order should not trigger Bitcoin refund.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: If Lightning already settled, voiding order does not reverse payment and needs separate refund.
claims.acceptance_test: Void unprepared open ticket; verify no payment record and reason logged; attempt post-prep state and require comp path.

claims.capability: Eligible restaurant sellers can reopen an unsettled closed check; setting controls whether original payment method is retained or removed/refunded.
claims.merchant_outcome: Corrects check contents/tip or wrong closure before settlement.
claims.trigger: Reopen closed check from Orders.
claims.behavior: Keep-payment option allows edit/re-close retaining method; remove-payment option removes original method and refunds original amount.
claims.preconditions: Restaurant Plus/Premium or advanced capability, proper modes/permissions, check not settled; POS iOS/Android Orders.
claims.qualifiers: US; can switch payment only before Close of Day or auto-settlement time when keep method enabled.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After settled/close-of-day cannot use documented reopen path; removing payment triggers refund.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose settlement deadline, refund consequence and retained authorization state before reopen.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin final settlement cannot be re-opened like a card authorization; OpenBMT should distinguish order edits from new Bitcoin refund payment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Keeping a card method preserves convenience; Bitcoin needs separate payment and may require liquidity/address confirmation.
claims.acceptance_test: Reopen an unsettled check under each mode; verify retained method vs refund and ensure settled check excluded.

claims.capability: Restaurant reopened checks with keep-payment enabled can auto-settle at end of reporting day, end of work day, or 36 hours after opening.
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant controls time for final settlement of open tipped checks.
claims.trigger: Configure automatic check settlement.
claims.behavior: Selectable settlement triggers include reporting day, workday close + 1.5 hours, or 36 hours after opening.
claims.preconditions: Reopen and Keep Payment Method enabled; Restaurant eligibility.
claims.qualifiers: US; timing affects when transfers/reporting finalize; longer 36-hour interval permits tips but delays funds.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Open checks settle automatically at configured time; tips after deadline may not be included.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make pending settlement volume and deadline visible and offer merchant-set timing.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Do not model Lightning payment as unsettled card authorization; settle Bitcoin when network payment received, handle later tip as separate transaction.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Separate tip invoice introduces extra customer step; include tip before Bitcoin payment when possible.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure each settlement schedule and verify when check finalizes and when tip entry stops.

claims.capability: Server can split a check by seat; seat-linked items move to individual checks and items assigned across seats divide evenly.
claims.merchant_outcome: Creates separate bills for diners by seating assignment.
claims.trigger: Select Split check > Split by seat.
claims.behavior: New checks are created for each occupied seat; table-level items may be moved manually; item-specific discounts/coupons/service charges follow item, cart-level amounts stay on original unless moved.
claims.preconditions: Seat tracking enabled for device; supported restaurant mode and plan.
claims.qualifiers: US; seat tracking required; source excludes fractional sell-by-unit items and portions of an already split item.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Reassign table-level items and cart-level charges manually; voiding one split fraction recombines item.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview each seat’s items, tax and shared charges before creating separate checks.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Keep seat allocation independent from Bitcoin payment; support one guest paying sats without changing other checks.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Separate payments and quotes per seat increase settlement steps; shared item arithmetic must be explicit.
claims.acceptance_test: Assign mixed seat/shared items and discount, split by seat, verify portions, item-level discounts and cart-level charges.

claims.capability: Qualified restaurant workflow can divide an individual item or all check items evenly or by custom amounts across checks and later recombine only under specified conditions.
claims.merchant_outcome: Supports shared-item bills without manual arithmetic.
claims.trigger: Select item split and choose even/custom portions.
claims.behavior: Split one item by number of ways or custom amounts; recombine during same split process or later only when all parts are returned to original check.
claims.preconditions: Restaurants Plus/Premium with New order and pay; item not sell-by-unit fractional or previously split portion.
claims.qualifiers: US; modifier cost cannot split below its parent item and is apportioned with item total.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Voiding any previously split item fraction automatically recombines item; constraints exclude certain items.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show portion lineage and make recombination state reversible while all fractions remain available.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Allow portions to be paid using different rails while preserving one item’s total and tax split.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Separate tender finality complicates recombination after a portion is already paid; require refund/payment adjustments.
claims.acceptance_test: Split shared item into thirds, pay one fraction, void another, and test recombination constraints and total conservation.

claims.capability: Restaurant staff can split a payment by amounts across multiple tenders; amount splitting does not allocate individual items.
claims.merchant_outcome: Lets multiple diners pay shares of one check with different methods.
claims.trigger: Choose split payment and enter payment amounts.
claims.behavior: Amount portions apply to one check; source says payment split is amount-only, distinct from check-by-item/seat.
claims.preconditions: Restaurant check/payment split supported; amount portions sum to full balance.
claims.qualifiers: US; card/tender restrictions may differ by hardware; Square general split tender has five-minute window.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Payment incomplete until full amount covered; restaurant article does not fully specify timeout details.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show remaining balance and tender status per payer, preserve item-level check as source of truth.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Support mixed Lightning/cash/card amounts with merchant-owned Bitcoin settlement and explicit finality per slice.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Different payment rails have distinct reversibility and quote timing; UI must reconcile asynchronous confirmations.
claims.acceptance_test: Split $100 check as $40/$60 using two tenders; verify amounts, remaining balance and completion only at zero.

claims.capability: Server can transfer one seat and its items to another check when a guest moves tables; the seat moves to a new seat at destination and may need item reassignment.
claims.merchant_outcome: Keeps guest order attached while table location changes.
claims.trigger: Seat menu > Transfer to Check; select destination check.
claims.behavior: Seat moves to new destination seat; items may be reassigned to new seat; full-table merge is separate and device restricted.
claims.preconditions: Seat tracking/check feature active; destination check available.
claims.qualifiers: US; merge tables feature requires Register; Terminal/Handheld can view merged tables.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Reassign items to destination seat when automatic mapping not desired.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preserve item/tax/discount associations during seat transfer and show confirmation of destination.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Payment address/Bitcoin invoice should not depend on a seat’s table assignment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: If transfer happens after payment request, cancel/reissue invoice with unchanged amount and clear status.
claims.acceptance_test: Transfer one seat with shared item and line discount; verify destination and seat-level allocation.

claims.capability: Restaurant operator can move items between courses or checks and move/merge an entire check/table before closure.
claims.merchant_outcome: Corrects ordering structure and combines or relocates checks during service.
claims.trigger: Select item or check and choose Move or merge action.
claims.behavior: Item can move to course/new/existing check; entire check can be moved into another check; floor-plan drag prompts merge confirmation when occupied.
claims.preconditions: Open Checks enabled; Restaurant POS; permission/passcode if moving another team member’s check.
claims.qualifiers: US; merging table from floor plan requires confirmation; terminal/handheld may view but not perform table merge.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If target occupied, confirm merge; exact post-payment move behavior is not covered by this page.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show impact on subtotal, seat allocation and payment state before merge.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Do not merge paid Bitcoin invoice states silently; preserve each settled receipt and add ledger adjustment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Moving already paid lines can require separate refund/new charge and accounting trail.
claims.acceptance_test: Move an unpaid item to existing check and merge whole checks; verify total conservation, confirmation and no duplicate payment.

claims.capability: A Restaurant check with cover count, even before items are added, persists on floor plan and makes the table appear occupied to hold it for arriving guests.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reserves table and creates an open service context before order entry.
claims.trigger: Set cover count on an open check.
claims.behavior: Check is saved and table appears occupied despite no cart items.
claims.preconditions: Open Checks enabled and Restaurant mode.
claims.qualifiers: US; seat count and cover count linked per seating settings; no payment yet.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Remove check/seat if guests do not arrive; void reason path for incorrect open tickets applies.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let merchant identify empty held check and expire/release it with audit record.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: OpenBMT payment demand/quote should not exist until payable cart is ready.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A held table is operational state, not a payment commitment; avoid generating Bitcoin invoices prematurely.
claims.acceptance_test: Set cover count with no items, leave and return to floor plan; verify persistence and occupied table; remove and verify release.

claims.capability: Cashier with transaction permissions can reprint paper receipt or send a new digital receipt from transaction history; gift receipt and declined card receipt have separate paths.
claims.merchant_outcome: Recovers proof after checkout without altering the underlying payment.
claims.trigger: Open transaction and choose New Receipt, Print Receipt, Print gift receipt or Send Receipt.
claims.behavior: POS reprint and Dashboard send use transaction history; resending does not alter automatic receipt settings; declined-payment print can be enabled via printer profile.
claims.preconditions: Transactions permission; compatible printer for printing.
claims.qualifiers: US; receipt paper/printer capability varies; digital recipient may be changed at sale receipt screen.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If original contact wrong, customer can supply new phone/email at receipt screen; resending does not alter opt-in settings.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make receipt resend separate from changing stored automatic receipt preference; retain audit log.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin receipt should be reproducible with payment hash/status and exchange rate, without exposing keys.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Lightning preimage/hash is sensitive operational data; expose only safe proof identifiers.
claims.acceptance_test: Reprint and resend same sale; verify no duplicate payment and automatic receipt preference unchanged.

claims.capability: Square may reuse opted-in customer receipt details across Square sellers; email or phone can be prepopulated on receipt screen, with phone masked for confirmation.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reduces repeated customer data entry for digital receipt.
claims.trigger: Previously opts in and pays another Square seller with same card/phone.
claims.behavior: Email may trigger automatic receipt with no prompt; stored phone appears redacted for customer confirmation.
claims.preconditions: Square receipt opt-in and recognized payment card/contact.
claims.qualifiers: US; customer is able to change contact at sale screen only when screen shown.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If skip receipt enabled, customer cannot edit/choose receipt at checkout.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let customer control receipt destination and avoid cross-merchant identity reuse by default.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Noncustodial Bitcoin payments should allow optional receipt address without requiring identity.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Requiring phone/email reduces privacy and can link wallet payments to identity.
claims.acceptance_test: Use opted-in card contact with receipt prompt on/off; verify reuse, masking, ability to change, and automatic-send behavior.

claims.capability: Reopen and Remove Payment Method removes original check payment and refunds original amount, while Reopen and Keep Payment Method retains the payment method for later recapture.
claims.merchant_outcome: Corrects closed check and can replace tender if not settled.
claims.trigger: Reopen check under chosen service setting.
claims.behavior: Remove-method path refunds original amount; keep-method path retains card and supports re-close or payment-method switch before settlement cutoff.
claims.preconditions: Eligible Restaurant capability, permission, unsettled check.
claims.qualifiers: US; check must not have reached close of day/automatic settlement for switching payment.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Refund and reprocess is needed if payment method is removed; direct behavior for non-card tender not established.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Label whether action will refund, preserve authorization or require new payment before confirmation.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: For settled Lightning payment, reopen changes order records only; issue a separate Bitcoin refund if merchant chooses.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A card payment may be reauthorized; Bitcoin receipt is irreversible and cannot be held open equivalently.
claims.acceptance_test: Reopen via keep and remove setting; verify card preserved or refunded, then change tender before auto-settlement.

claims.capability: Square payment terms state a card refund/adjustment must include associated taxes required to be refunded and cannot exceed original total.
claims.merchant_outcome: Sets an accounting constraint on returns.
claims.trigger: Process refund/adjustment for card sale.
claims.behavior: Payment terms require associated refundable tax to be included; POS help allows itemized or amount refunds without detailing exact tax math.
claims.preconditions: Square card payment terms; legal/tax rules applicable to merchant.
claims.qualifiers: US; legal terms are general card payment terms; merchant still responsible for applicable tax compliance.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Use transaction detail and local tax rules; gaps between POS UI and policy documentation remain.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview item, discount and tax allocation; surface tax requirement with itemized refund.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Refund Bitcoin sale with a new payment and keep original tax amount in merchant accounting record.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Fiat-equivalent tax accounting can differ from current BTC amount paid back.
claims.acceptance_test: Refund taxable sale and compare refund amount against original tax and payment terms; verify required tax included.

claims.capability: Merchant can include refund/return policy on email, text and printed receipts; if no policy is present, Square says it is assumed there is no policy.
claims.merchant_outcome: Shows buyer the merchant’s return terms after purchase.
claims.trigger: Configure receipt policy; buyer receives receipt.
claims.behavior: Receipt policy appears in digital and paper receipt; absence implies no policy per Square help.
claims.preconditions: Receipt settings configured in Dashboard.
claims.qualifiers: US; terms should be clearly stated; legal sufficiency not assessed.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Update receipt policy if business rules change; existing receipts retain historic policy.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Keep policy concise and accessible before payment as well as on receipt.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin refunds require clear disclosure that transfer is final and refund is a new transaction/store credit.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Policy must distinguish card reversal and Bitcoin return path.
claims.acceptance_test: Set return policy and verify on email/text/print receipts; remove it and verify no policy appears.

claims.capability: Eligible Square Bitcoin sellers can choose to receive Bitcoin payments as Bitcoin credited to Square Bitcoin wallet or USD credited to Square balance; USD option converts incoming Bitcoin at then-effective rate.
claims.merchant_outcome: Selects the settlement denomination for accepted Lightning Bitcoin sales.
claims.trigger: During Bitcoin payments setup, choose Bitcoin or dollar settlement.
claims.behavior: Square Terms specify incoming Bitcoin is either credited to Square Bitcoin wallet on confirmation, less fees, or automatically converted to USD at Block’s then-effective market rate and credited to Square balance.
claims.preconditions: Square Bitcoin enabled for eligible account and location; business verification and applicable setup completed.
claims.qualifiers: US eligible sellers, no New York; terms last updated 2026-03-16. Bitcoin-in-wallet settlement means Square custody while funds remain in that wallet (see SQC-C023).
