claims.recovery_edge_cases: Conversion rates and settlement times may vary due to market/network/technical factors. Documentation does not promise any particular exchange rate.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Offer direct merchant-controlled Bitcoin settlement as the default, with USD conversion as an optional merchant-selected flow.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: OpenBMT should make settlement currency and any fiat conversion explicit; default can be Bitcoin to merchant keys with optional third-party conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: USD conversion lowers seller BTC exposure but adds conversion spread/counterparty; Bitcoin settlement preserves BTC but requires merchant custody, accounting and volatility management.
claims.acceptance_test: On eligible setup, select Bitcoin then USD settlement in separate test profiles; verify the displayed destination, conversion disclosure and settlement ledger outcome.

claims.capability: Square wallet user can request a Bitcoin withdrawal to an external wallet address, choosing a withdrawal speed, completing two-factor authentication and confirming; limits and review may apply.
claims.merchant_outcome: Moves Bitcoin from Square custody to a merchant-controlled external wallet.
claims.trigger: In Square Dashboard Bitcoin section, enter amount/address, choose speed and confirm withdrawal.
claims.behavior: Wallet support docs list standard (24 hours or less), rush (2 hours or less) and priority (10 minutes or less) options, require two-factor authentication, and state daily and weekly withdrawal limits; legal terms state verification/security screening can delay or restrict withdrawals and an initiated withdrawal cannot be reversed.
claims.preconditions: Eligible Square wallet account; available Bitcoin; valid external address; 2FA; withdrawal feature available.
claims.qualifiers: US; not available to New York or US territories. Help page limits are $15,000/day and $50,000/week; fees depend on speed. These are wallet withdrawals, not direct POS settlement to a merchant wallet.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Confirm address carefully; withdrawal may be held for verification/security review or delayed by network; once initiated, cannot be reversed. Wallet support article and Terms differ on whether external wallet deposits are currently available; this claim is withdrawal only.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Avoid requiring custodial withdrawal as an intermediate step by supporting direct settlement to the merchant’s own wallet.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: OpenBMT should let a merchant choose and verify its own wallet at setup, then receive directly without Square-controlled withdrawal limits or custody.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Direct self-custody eliminates withdrawal delay but makes key management, address safety and network fee policy the merchant’s responsibility.
claims.acceptance_test: Verify destination-address confirmation, 2FA, available speed/fee/limit display, pending review state, and irreversibility after request submission.

limitations: Research is documented-only; product compatibility and checkout success were not tested.

The research pass did not verify exact US official support sections for tax calculation, tip prompts, standard receipt dispatch, standard void/refund workflow, payment void eligibility, or Restaurant check split edge cases; listed topics remain unresolved/partially documented.
Square support pages sometimes describe dynamic 2026 rollout and fee language. Recheck these values as of implementation time, especially BTC limits, eligible account defaults and fee schedule.

Bitcoin custody is classified as Square-mediated/custodial based on Square wallet setup and no merchant key-control evidence in the inspected support page; this is a qualified interpretation, not an independent technical custody audit.
No claims are made about Square’s APIs, merchant banking, card processing SDKs, catalog/inventory/customer/staff/drawer/reporting/hardware capabilities beyond checkout-relevant qualifiers.
Several related source pages surfaced in search but were not fully inspected; unsupported claims were left unresolved rather than inferred from missing documentation.
